Implement GitHub issue #23 — "Two messages can start two chat children on one conversation".
https://github.com/Xapicc/UsageFoundry/issues/23

In `src/lib/chat.ts`, the "is this chat already thinking?" check is separated from the write that records it by an `await` that performs a full transcript scan. Two messages sent into one chat inside that window both start a billed `claude` child on the same conversation.

Done looks like: the check and the claim are atomic, so the second concurrent message is rejected rather than spawning a second child, and there is a regression test that fails before the change and passes after — one that would still catch the race if the interleaving changed. Every acceptance-criteria box in the issue holds.

Scope note: issues #19, #20, #22 and #25 are also open against `src/lib/chat.ts` and may be running in parallel on their own branches. This one is in `sendChatMessage` rather than `runTurn`, so keep the diff there and minimal, and note anything adjacent in your report instead of fixing it.
finalText:
Committed on `uf/usagefoundry-13-c55bc71b` as `906a505`.

## What changed

**`src/lib/chat.ts`** — `sendChatMessage`'s check-then-act became a claim. New private `claimTurn(chatId)` runs `UPDATE chat_sessions SET status='thinking', error=NULL, updated_at=? WHERE id=? AND status<>'thinking'` and returns the row only when `changes === 1`; the caller returns the "still working on the last message" refusal otherwise. The claim sits *after* `await assistRefusal()` (that gate is untouched, per the out-of-scope note) and there is no `await` between it and the spawn, so appending the user message, reading the history and starting the child are all one event-loop turn. The turn now uses the row as it stood at the claim rather than the pre-`await` read — `session_id` off a stale read is what decides whether the turn resumes or pays to replay the thread. The condition is `<> 'thinking'`, not `= 'idle'`, so a chat left `failed` by a bad turn is still retryable.

**`src/lib/chat.test.ts`** — the file now sets `DATA_DIR`/`CLAUDE_HOME`/`CLAUDE_BIN` into a temp dir and `require`s `./chat` (the pattern `orchestrator.test.ts` already uses, since imports hoist above env setup), and replaces `child_process.spawn` with a counter returning a fake child. Three tests added; the existing pure tests are unchanged.

**`CLAUDE.md`** — the `npm test` inventory now names the turn claim, and says plainly that this one test is neither a pure function nor a rendering, with the argument for why it clears the bar.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Two concurrent POSTs → one child, loser refused** — the race test drives two `sendChatMessage` calls into the `assistRefusal()` window and asserts `spawnCount` rose by exactly 1, one outcome `ok`, the other matching `/still working on the last message/`. `src/app/api/chat/[id]/message/route.ts:23` already turns that reason into a 400, so the loser's request answers with it.
- **Claim is a conditional UPDATE whose `changes` decides** — `claimTurn`, `src/lib/chat.ts:604`.
- **Loser appends no user message** — asserted: exactly one `role === "user"` message in the thread after the race.
- **Regression test failing before, passing after** — confirmed both directions. Against `HEAD~1`'s `chat.ts` (test file kept): `not ok 1 - starts one child when two messages race into one chat … a second child must not be spawned / 2 !== 1`. With the fix: all pass. The load-bearing assertion is the child count, not the interleaving, so a different resume order still fails it.

## Verification

```
NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev   → ok
npm run typecheck                            → ok (tsc --noEmit, no output)
npm test                                     → 223 tests, 223 pass, 0 fail
```

Pre-fix run of the new tests: `# tests 25 / # pass 24 / # fail 1` — the failure being the race test.

**Not run here:** the issue's two-curl reproduction. It needs a live server (`docker compose up --build`, or `npm run dev`), which this container cannot do, and under the pre-fix code it spawns two real billed children. A human can check it with the issue's snippet; `ps -eo args | grep -c '[c]laude -p'` should rise by one and the second POST should return HTTP 400 with `{"error":"This chat is still working on the last message."}`.

## Noted, not touched

The fake-`spawn` harness patches a module-global for the whole file — safe because `node --test` runs each test file in its own process, but it does mean anything added to `chat.test.ts` later inherits it.

One adjacent hazard I left alone, in `runTurn`/`finishTurn` rather than `sendChatMessage`: `finishTurn` writes `status` unconditionally, so a turn landing late (e.g. a timed-out child that exits after the row was already reconciled) can still put a chat back to `idle`. The claim now makes that unreachable via this path, since no second turn can start, but the write itself is still unguarded.

DONE
